_comment: TEST FIXTURE — not a live config. This is the evenplay-mono rule table as
validated against 98 real PR merges on 2026-07-31, kept here so the tests
assert real-world behaviour deterministically. The LIVE copy lives in the
project itself at evenplay-mono/.claude/risk-paths.json — the rule table is
project-specific and does not belong in this shared tooling repo.
as of 2026-07-29 (apps/finance-domain/{wallet,paygate}, apps/game-domain/
{challenge,engine,paylines,station-state-computer}, apps/platform-domain/
{backoffice,bay-session,cloud-frs,core,league,notifications,partner-service}).
SEMANTICS — monotone, max-wins, union. A file may match many rules:
risk       = MAX over every matched rule (low < medium < high < critical)
components = UNION over every matched rule
financial  = OR  over every matched rule
presentation = a file is presentational only if EVERY rule it matched is
marked presentation; one non-presentation match disqualifies it
Adding a rule can therefore only ever RAISE risk. Rule order is irrelevant.
A file matching NO rule takes unmatched_risk and is listed in
classification.unmatched_files. That is the fail-closed default: a new
directory nobody has classified yet reviews HIGH until a rule is added.
Components must be one of the presets cmd/reviewer's componentFloorPresets
accepts: wallet, bet-settlement, bet-placement, jackpot, responsible-gambling.
cmd/classify rejects unknown component names at config load, so a typo cannot
reach the reviewer. Floors are NOT computed here — cmd/reviewer's buildFloors
owns them; duplicating the table would let the two drift.
Glob syntax: '**' matches zero or more path segments; '*' and '?' match within
one segment. Paths are repo-root-relative, forward slashes.

rules.note: Balance mutations, payout claims, ledger. The money core.
Payment gateway + transactor — external money movement.
accept_bet / wager / arm / bet-amount bounds — money in.
Settlement, hole-in-one settlement, settle SQL — money out.
Dispute reversal and force-refund — operator-initiated money movement.
Replay/retry of financial + state-mutation operations (pr-raise.md rule 1).
Payout rules, prize/tournament payout tables — outcome-to-money mapping.
Payline evaluation — gambling outcome determination (Critical per tier table).
Shared money library used by every service. Found unclassified by the 60-PR validation sweep on 2026-07-31 — it was taking the fail-closed high tier with no component preset and no financial flag.
Shared authorization and capability gates — fail-open here is systemic.
Remaining shared Go libraries: errcodes, logging, asyncfetch, workerpool, address.

Client-side withdrawal, wallet, deposit and card-entry surfaces. NOT presentation: these display balances and submit money movements, and PR 1294's escaped regression was a display bug. The 60-PR sweep found PR 1262 (40 files, native card tokenization) and PR 1350 (43 files, autoplay wager preference) both taking the single-reviewer carve-out because every path sat under src/ — this rule closes that. panel_floor=full: medium risk alone would under-panel a money surface.
Kubernetes manifests and environment config — a bad value here is a production incident.
Generated protobuf clients shipped into the mobile app. Wire contract, never presentation.
Backtesting and calibration for paylines/stake weighting. Not production-serving, but it is where game-math parameters are derived.
Repo-root Playwright cross-app suite (the apps/*/e2e rule below only covers per-app harnesses).
Bet limits, autoplay limits, confidence-bet limits, practice/tournament exclusion.
Rest of the bet/session state machine. High by default; the rules above raise the money paths to Critical.
Engine + station state computer — state machines, wallet RPC clients.
Core platform services and DAOs.
Auth, OTP, rate limiting, session issuance — server side.
Any migration or raw SQL. Loads migration-checklist.md deterministically.
Protos and generated stubs — cross-service contract, never client-only.
Client auth surface — NOT presentation; token handling is a security surface.
Presentation-only client code. The ONLY reduced-panel carve-out — and only when no gate signal fires and nothing above matched.
Test harnesses and mock services.
Deployment/infra config — cannot be presentation, cannot be low.
CI workflows and repo scripts. Not presentation — scripts/check-migration-ordering.sh IS a gate, and a change here can disable a check rather than fail one.
Dependency changes are supply-chain surface — never low.

gate_signals.note: Environment-driven behaviour switch — the PR 1298 fail-open class.
Build-mode gate. Ships enabled if the flag leaks to a deployed env.
Feature flag / kill switch — decides whether something is allowed or shown.

Explicit skip/bypass DECISION sites. Deliberately narrow: an earlier pattern matched [Oo]verride[A-Z_] and force[A-Z], which fired on 39% of PRs because this codebase has an admin-override FEATURE — OverrideRequest, override_by, override_at are proto types and DB columns, not gate decisions. Matching domain nouns costs the signal its meaning; match the verbs.
Real-money vs practice mode decision — money exposure if it fails open.
